Bystrytsya Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bystrytsia, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1918 per epigraphic data, presumably used until WWII, with its latest preserved gravestone dated 1939. Jews are believed to have arrived in the first half of the 18th century; population reached 57 by 1880, rising to 150 by 1910 and settling at 139 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period, of 999 total residents). Population reached 151 by 1930. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; some Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. A number of Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; remaining Bystrytsia Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
